findings.title: Underwater withdraw buffer is FCFS at par, socializing strategy loss onto slow stakers
findings.triageReason: Intended design (confirmed by protocol owner). The underwater buffer pays daily-volume withdrawals at par during transient, mean-reverting underwater dips to avoid sparking panic and to avoid forcing users to realise losses by redeeming shares at the bottom; bank-run / mass-exit is handled separately by migrateOut with pro-rata distribution. The report itself concedes there is no incremental victim (the slow staker is baseline-unchanged vs a no-buffer world). The buffer-at-par path implements the documented invariant 'a non-migrating user cannot be forced to realise a loss', and both of the finding's recommended fixes (block the buffer branch / pro-rata haircut) would defeat that design goal. Reclassified from Medium to intended-design via /review-finding.

findings.title: Terminal migration has no mint-free escape hatch if phUSD minter rights are revoked mid-migration
findings.triageReason: Intended design (user triage 2026-06-08, via /review-finding ss7m3). emergencyWithdraw/withdraw/deposit are deliberately frozen once migrationInfo[token].active because initiateMigration captures an immutable (R,P) snapshot and every exit pays a fixed pro-rata credit p_i*min(R,P)/P; a live exit during migration would mutate P and corrupt the snapshot (StableStaker.sol:306-307, 335-340). The Law-2 'faithfulness gap' framing is therefore invalid. The residual 'revoke staker's phUSD minter while migration active -> exits revert' sliver is an obvious admin misstep (Law 3 out-of-scope) and recoverable. Not submittable.
findings.proposalResolution: REJECTED 2026-06-08 — finding triaged wont-fix as intended design; proposed Medium not applied.
findings.description: During an active terminal migration, emergencyWithdraw is blocked (migration active), and the only exits (userMigrate, batchMigrate) mint frozen pending phUSD via _exitPosition -> phUSD.mint BEFORE transferring principal. If the staker loses phUSD minter rights while a token is active, those exits revert on the pending-phUSD mint and principal is retrievable only after minter rights are restored. Healthy mode has a mint-free escape (emergencyWithdraw); terminal mode does not. Bounded by the owner-trusted precondition 'minter revoked mid-migration'.
findings.impact: Owner-trust-bounded availability: principal is not permanently lost, but is temporarily unrecoverable from terminal-migration exits until phUSD minter rights are restored.

findings.triageReason: Acknowledged (user triage 2026-06-08, via /review-finding ss7m4). Finding is VALID and stays at Medium: the underwater buffer-path withdraw genuinely desyncs totalStaked < strategy.principalOf and bricks initiateMigration's L392 full-drain post-check (PoC passes). Accepted-not-fixed because the clean root fix is CROSS-CUTTING across two submodules: it requires a new client-callable RELINQUISH-PRINCIPAL primitive on the yield strategy (reduce clientBalances[token][client] and totalDeposited by the buffer-paid amount WITHOUT redeeming shares) added to reflax-yield-vault's IYieldStrategy + ERC4626YieldStrategy, plus a stable-staker buffer-branch call into it. This is finding Option A formalized. Beyond un-bricking migration it reconciles principalOf==totalStaked at source AND correctly surfaces post-recovery over-collateralization as skimmable surplus -> yield to stable-yield-accumulator (the relinquished shares stay in the strategy, repurposed from principal-backing to surplus-backing; totalValue unchanged, totalDeposited drops, surplus rises by exactly the relinquished amount). Re point-1 (donation-funded buffer): NOT an exploit vector — a donation lands in the staker's idle balance, never touches the strategy's clientBalances/totalDeposited/totalValue, and relinquish only fires when a real user claim is extinguished, so it cannot be pumped; freed value is honest over-collateralization (at worst spreads to co-clients of a SHARED strategy via pooled accounting, harming no claimholder; avoidable with a dedicated strategy). Re point-3 (par-vs-haircut fairness): already covered — withdraw reverts while underwater except through the reserve buffer (by design), residual FCFS is the wont-fix 'underwater buffer FCFS at par' M and the M-05 emergencyWithdraw family. Fix is design-level/cross-submodule, not a one-line staker patch.
findings.fixVerification: VERIFIED-FIXED at stable-staker-08 (HEAD f85450b). story-007 landed the cross-submodule relinquishPrincipal primitive (declared IYieldStrategy L41, implemented AYieldStrategy._relinquishInternal) and wired the stable-staker buffer branch to call strategy.relinquishPrincipal(token, amount) at StableStaker.sol:703 — reducing principal WITHOUT redeeming shares, so principalOf == totalStaked is preserved through a buffer-path withdraw and initiateMigration's L392 full-drain post-check is once again satisfiable. PoC-replay PoC_M04_BufferDesyncBricksMigration.t.sol LIKELY-FIXED: a migration that previously bricked now succeeds with principalOf == 70 == totalStaked. This was the user's primary audit driver. Owner had acknowledged with the Option-A cross-submodule fix as the accepted path; that fix has now landed, so status flips acknowledged -> fixed with evidence (consistent with the owner's stated intent, not a silent overwrite).

findings.title: Migration credit asymmetry: operator batchMigrate books users below principal through a haircutting destination strategy while userMigrate keeps full value

Magnitude = destination slippageToleranceBps; zero when the destination is idle/full-credit at migration time.

findings.description: The socialization (p_i*min(R,P)/P when R<P) is INTENDED/faithful (story-003/004, StableStaker.sol:527-528), NOT a bug. The footgun: the in-place initiateMigration flow is not blocked on an impaired strategy and gives no migrator-side signal, so an operator reaching for a 'safe rewire' tool silently crystallizes the underwater delta on live stakers. Distinct from KI#6 / 69c7666e (that is _routeExit buffer-at-par FCFS).
findings.impact: No new value bug. Law-3 operator footgun; deliverable is safe-config guidance (check withdrawDisabled/_isUnderwater before the in-place flow; route impaired strategies through the cross-staker terminal path).

findings.label: L-03
findings.title: Revived-pool permissionless-stake window before migrateIn (exploit refuted; emission-dilution only)
findings.lawBasis: Law-3 operational footgun; exploit angle REFUTED (kept in visible channel per Law 1).
findings.description: After finalizeAndReset the empty pool is Active and stake is permissionless before migrateIn runs; an interloper can stake first. Theft/inflation/rate-manipulation REFUTED (MasterChef accumulator accPhusdPerShare/rewardDebt, not totalAssets share price; parked principal unreachable; migrateIn credits each user their own pinned amt). Sole residual: emission-share dilution (normal MasterChef TVL dilution of in-motion/unmatured yield, not a leak).
findings.impact: None to principal; emission-dilution only. Same revival-runbook surface as ss9l1 (stale-config) and ss10l1 (dust-stake gate-grief); distinct root cause. Recommend pause-wrapping the out->reset->rewire->in session; consider bundling with ss9l1/ss10l1 under one 'revival-window pause-wrap' QA recommendation.

findings.label: L-04
findings.title: Near-MIN_TIMEOUT multi-batch self-exit leaves a partially-refilled pool
findings.description: If migrationTimeout is sized near MIN_TIMEOUT (1 day) and a multi-batch rewire stalls past it, parked users can claimTimedOut mid-migration (full principal, self-exit); the later migrateIn slice skips them (amt==0 -> continue, InPlaceMigrator.sol:210), leaving a partially-refilled pool. Docs scope OUT many-batch jobs (InPlaceMigrator.sol:54-55) as a recommendation, not an enforced bound. Emission-cap integrity and force-timeout incentive separately refuted; completeness is the sole residual.
findings.impact: No value lost; every user keeps full principal. Migration completeness only. Recommend sizing migrationTimeout above the full out->reset->in duration (7-day default is sound).

findings.label: L-01
findings.title: InPlaceMigrator.migrateIn surplus-underfunding batch revert + no cross-slice surplus reservation
findings.description: story-013's gross-up top-up math (topup = mulDiv(amt - credited, amt, credited), :276) silently introduces a surplus pre-funding requirement invisible at the call site: the operator must pre-fund grossed-up surplus over and above parked principal, or a migrateIn slice through a haircutting strategy fails require(topup <= balanceOf - totalParked) (:280-281) and the whole batch reverts atomically. Greedy earlier slices can also exhaust the shared surplus, stranding later paginated slices (no per-slice reservation). Folds CODE-002: the require subtracts balanceOf - totalParked (:281), underflowing to panic 0x11 instead of a readable revert. AVAILABILITY/QA residue of the story-013 ss12m1 fix; atomic revert (no value loss), recoverable via claimTimedOut. Law-3 footgun.
findings.impact: No principal loss. Atomic revert; migration DEFERRED not DoS'd (retryable + permissionless self-scoped claimTimedOut). Law-3 non-obvious operator footgun (undocumented gross-up surplus pre-funding step).

findings.label: L-02
findings.title: InPlaceMigrator.rescueERC20 vs top-up budget coupling can brick par-restoration mid-migration
findings.description: rescueERC20 (:337-339) and the _reinjectWithTopup surplus budget (:280-281) draw from the SAME unescrowed balanceOf - totalParked quantity. An owner who pre-funds surplus then sweeps 'stray' balance via rescueERC20 mid-migration unknowingly removes the in-flight top-up budget and triggers the ss13l1 revert on the next slice. Non-obvious: the NatSpec advertises the principal floor (totalParked) as untouchable, so a sweep fenced above it reads safe yet bricks an in-progress migration. Pattern-parallel to ledger 0790a76a (StableStaker.rescueERC20 sweeps underwater buffer) but distinct contract/reserve/fingerprint.
findings.impact: No principal loss (totalParked intact); only an in-progress migration stalls, backstopped by claimTimedOut. Law-3 non-obvious inter-function coupling footgun.

findings.label: L-03
findings.title: InPlaceMigrator._reinjectWithTopup small-principal top-up truncation reverts the migrateIn batch
findings.description: Two compounding integer-truncation facets. CODE-001: when shortfall grosses up to topup == 0 (mulDiv floors, :276), depositFor(token, user, 0) hits require(amount > 0) and reverts the atomic batch; the if (credited < amt) predicate (:273) is misaligned with depositFor's >0 precondition so control never reaches the finalCredited backstop (:288-292). CODE-004: for amt < 1000 units, amt/1000 == 0 collapses require(finalCredited >= amt - amt/1000) (:292) to zero-tolerance exact-par; round-down gross-up leaves finalCredited a few wei short -> revert. The advertised 0.1% slack evaporates below amt=1000. Distinct from KI#2 (silent reward dust round-DOWN; this is a REVERT on the migration path).
findings.impact: No principal loss. Atomic revert on sub-1000-unit dust migrateIn slices; implementation-quality/availability arithmetic defect, not an owner action or theft path.

findings.label: L-04
findings.title: InPlaceMigrator.migrateIn dangling forceApprove(staker, balanceOf) contradicts the in-code comment
findings.description: Code-vs-comment contradiction (not a faithfulness F-XX — it is a code-vs-in-code-comment mismatch, not a [story-NNN] deviation). NatSpec at :190-192 claims forceApprove is set to the EXACT slice total and 'never left dangling ... nothing lingers'; code at :225-226 approves balanceOf(address(this)) > total + Sigma topup, leaving a residual allowance to staker. The comment's invariant is false as written.
findings.impact: None. Residual allowance granted to the immutable, trusted staker; next migrateIn overwrites (no monotonic accumulation). Documentation/hygiene defect surfaced in a visible QA channel (Law-1 recall-beats-tidiness).
